metadata.title: Assessing quality of life in Mahmudia Commune (Danube Delta): a socio-territorial analysis based on local population perceptions
metadata.description:
Deltaic regions represent complex socio-ecological systems where biodiversity conservation objectives must be balanced with the need to improve the living conditions of local communities. Despite the protected status of the Danube Delta since the establishment of the Biosphere Reserve, human activities and socio-economic transformations have significantly influenced both ecosystem functioning and local livelihoods. However, assessments of quality of life in relation to sustainable development and local community perspectives remain limited.

This study aims to evaluate the quality of life perceived by the local population of Mahmudia commune, located within the Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve, and to identify the main socio-economic vulnerabilities and development opportunities. The research combines objective socio-economic indicators with subjective assessments obtained through a questionnaire survey applied to 90 residents in 2023. The evaluation considered multiple dimensions of quality of life, including financial conditions, housing, household goods, basic needs, social integration, community environment, local governance and development priorities.

The results highlight a complex situation characterized by significant demographic decline, limited employment opportunities, especially for young people, and concerns regarding future socio-economic development. At the same time, the community benefits from important social resources, including strong interpersonal relationships, community cohesion and a positive perception of local safety. The findings indicate that improving quality of life in Mahmudia requires integrated development strategies that address economic and social vulnerabilities while maintaining compatibility with the conservation objectives of the Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve.

The study contributes to a better understanding of quality of life in protected rural areas by emphasizing the importance of incorporating local perceptions into sustainable development policies and decision-making processes.

metadata.description: Objetivo: avaliar a influência de três ângulos de incidência luminosa (90°, 45° e 30°) sobre a dureza superficial de uma resina composta. Métodos: estudo experimental laboratorial com 45 corpos de prova de resina Opallis A2D (FGM), distribuídos em três grupos independentes (n = 15). A fotoativação ocorreu por 40 segundos com aparelho Radii-Cal (SDI) em suporte padronizador. Foram utilizadas exclusivamente as 45 leituras originais da tabela de resultados, informadas na escala Rockwell HR30T. Empregaram-se estatística descritiva, Shapiro–Wilk, Levene, ANOVA de um fator, ANOVA de Welch, Kruskal–Wallis e Tukey (α = 0,05). Resultados: as médias (± DP) foram 45,65 ± 3,79 (90°), 40,97 ± 2,65 (45°) e 29,82 ± 4,45 (30°) HR30T. A ANOVA indicou diferença global (F(2,42) = 72,3741; p = 2,47 × 10⁻¹⁴), confirmada por Welch (p = 3,11 × 10⁻¹⁰) e Kruskal–Wallis (p = 7,83 × 10⁻⁸). O teste de Tukey apontou diferenças em todos os pares (p ajustado ≤ 0,0035). Conclusão: nas condições experimentais, menores ângulos em relação à superfície acompanharam menores leituras de dureza; os achados não medem diretamente conversão monomérica ou longevidade clínica.

STARLI  /  WHITE RAINBOW EPOCH

WHEN A NEURAL INTERFACE MUST PROVE ITS MATERIAL IDENTITY

A Scientific Field Notebook on Nanomaterial Charge Transfer, Flexible Conductors, Tissue Compatibility, and the Boundary of Durable Neural Recording

FLAGSHIP FAMILY F001–F010

Author: 33 × STARLI  |  Scientific Field Notebook v1.0  |  08 November 2026

A continuous, evidence-centered English reading route across ten prospective 777-page STARLI/YULI research monographs. This narrative is a scholarly interpretation and future experimental design, not a report of executed experiments or a therapeutic efficacy claim.

THE CORE QUESTION

What does it mean for a neural-interface material to remain the same functional object when it is wetted, bent, contaminated, damaged, aged, and finally retired?

READER’S ROADMAP

Read the first two notes as the scientific framing, then follow ten flagship investigations and their connecting interludes. The final notes bring the mechanism claims back to blind falsification, Research Gates and external research succession. Every trial scene is hypothetical unless explicitly identified as a sourced method proposal.

SOURCE AND SCIENTIFIC POSITION

The scene in this notebook is a laboratory that has not yet run the complete experiment. The samples, observations, laboratory disagreements and blinded trials described as scenes are explicitly hypothetical examples of how the proposed programs could be evaluated. That distinction is essential. The ten source volumes are research-design working editions, not executed trial reports and not evidence of therapeutic efficacy. Their contribution is a set of questions with units, controls, limits, adversarial tests and future research interfaces.

A productive scientific story starts with uncertainty. To understand a new mechanism, the researcher must first know which ordinary mechanism would be mistaken for it. To trust a measurement, the researcher must know where its reference came from. To believe an advantage, the researcher must know which samples were excluded and whether an equally competent conventional design could have performed as well. To call an intervention safe, the researcher must know which negative condition forces the study to stop. These are the reasons this notebook moves between theory, experiment, counterexample and decision.

The following narrative draws its flagship titles, core research boundaries, primary measurands, comparator concepts, blinded challenges and stopping criteria from the supplied STARLI/YULI family ZIP. Technical explanations and illustrative trial designs expand that material for readers, but they do not silently supply empirical results absent from the originals. The source PDFs contain 30 research formula plates, 82 chapters, 410 investigation pages, 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix proposal pages per volume. The scale is remarkable, but a large number of pages must never be confused with the number of independent established discoveries.

FIELD NOTE 01 | WHY THIS FAMILY EXISTS

It asks whether an independent group can reproduce the proposed change in conductance recovery [%] after concealed crack orientation while giving apparent recovery due to parallel shunt, electrode relocation or transient wet contact a fair chance to explain the same observations. FIELD NOTE 09 | F008 — Signal-Selective Neural Nanomaterials At The Limit

Recovery can become dangerous if it creates a conductive shortcut. Similarly, selectivity can become misleading if the analysis computer creates a discrimination that the material itself never achieved. Both chapters ask which component of the apparatus deserves credit.

Signal selectivity is often confused with excellent signal processing. A material that favors one frequency band must be compared with an ordinary electrode followed by a competent filter. Otherwise the apparent nanomaterial advantage may belong to the analysis code. Target-to-off-target amplitude ratio in decibels gives a useful endpoint only if the definition of the target, the irrelevant sources and the amplifier chain are fixed before testing.

The first measurement contract is deceptively strict. Write the quantity of interest on the protocol cover, including its unit: target-to-offtarget amplitude ratio [dB]. Identify its experimental unit, which is not automatically the individual frame, a single cell, or a repeated instrument reading. Decide whether normalization changes the scientific question. A ratio can hide an unstable denominator; a percentage can rise when the underlying population shrinks; a time-to-failure can look impressive if early failures are censored. That is why the proposed signal-selective neural nanomaterials at the limit experiment has to publish its numerator, denominator, censoring convention and uncertainty budget along with its final number. No beautiful image or smooth curve should be allowed to choose the metric after the labels are unsealed.

A blind target-band exchange deliberately changes which band counts as relevant. The material's physical transfer function and the downstream digital selection must be recorded separately. If a signal can be rescued only after investigators choose a favorable filter, the evidence does not support intrinsic material selectivity. Unexpected motion artifacts and electrical stimulation leakage provide additional negative controls.

Before anyone celebrates, invite a plausible conventional model into the room. In this topic it is selectivity created by post-hoc signal filtering, frequency imbalance or altered amplifier gain. Design the experiment so that the rival can predict a genuine held-out observation, then compare the proposed mechanism with matched passive electrode with conventional analogue/digital bandpass filtering. Match ordinary confounders first, but avoid 'correcting away' the physical difference that the hypothesis is supposed to explain. This distinction between legitimate nuisance adjustment and over-adjustment must be specified before the experiment runs. If both models perform equally well, the responsible claim is uncertainty, not a dramatic declaration of novel physics.

The concealed challenge in the source is blind target-band exchange. Its scientific value is that it attacks the privileged information of the investigator. The researcher must freeze the prediction before discovering which material or culture condition received the change. A blinded challenge is not simply a shuffled label; it must be technically strong enough to alter a causal pathway that the proposed mechanism claims to understand. An independent witness should verify that the perturbation actually occurred while guarding against accidental disclosure. If the entire effect disappears at unblinding, the failure belongs in the primary result rather than an appendix of inconvenient details.

The explicit hard-stop boundary in this source is false target identification, stimulation leakage, thermal burden or unreliable false-positive control. A stop condition is not an editorial disclaimer. It is a causal part of the experiment because the most attractive observation may occur in a specimen that has already ceased to satisfy the integrity conditions under which the hypothesis was stated. For this chapter, the stop log should be evaluated before computing any favorable average. The point is not to make promising material development impossible, but to prevent an uncontrolled risk or a broken measurement reference from being renamed a technical success.

The receiving laboratory should acquire raw unfiltered waveforms, hardware response curves, gain logs, band labels under seal and the analysis code. It must calculate sensitivity and false-positive rate on a truly held-out source mixture. The decisive discovery could be that the cheaper passive electrode with orthodox filtering is entirely sufficient.

For publication, the record should be split into raw observations, qualified derived measurements, model outputs and interpretive claims. A value of target-to-offtarget amplitude ratio [dB] belongs in the second layer only when the reference materials, instruments and sample identity are traceable. Model outputs belong in the third layer; they are not silently promoted to measured facts. The final claim is then constrained by which layers survived blind perturbation and independent reanalysis. A Gate is useful when a future scientist can answer it with a decisive 'no.' In this case the falsifier is a frozen prediction about target-to-offtarget amplitude ratio [dB] during blind target-band exchange. A second Gate tests the transfer of that prediction to a new batch or laboratory. A third records the point at which the claim must be abandoned because selectivity created by post-hoc signal filtering, frequency imbalance or altered amplifier gain predicts the evidence equally well. What survives should be archived with the failed experiments. A Phoenix proposal can make the next test easier, but cannot substitute a successful prototype for the evidence that prototype would still need.

FIELD NOTE 10 | F009 — Long-Term Stable Neural Nanoimplant Materials At The Limit

Longevity is an argument about time and a distribution of failures, not an attractive specimen that survived. Impedance drift can arise from corrosion, delamination, ionic infiltration, insulation leakage or biological fouling. Accelerated ageing is tempting because it compresses time, but a harsh condition can create a failure mechanism that never dominates in ordinary use. The source makes time-to-impedance-failure its explicit endpoint.

An experimental notebook should follow the evidence through time. The target measure, time-to-impedance-failure [day], is only one member of a sequence beginning at specimen preparation and ending at an independently verifiable physical or biological state. At each step, save the source observations rather than only their processed summary. Separate within-specimen repetition from true independent material lots; maintain calibration histories; carry failed specimens into the analysis. For long-term stable neural nanoimplant materials at the limit, an unexplained change in sample composition or geometry could imitate the desired effect. A serious design therefore records nuisance information before anyone knows whether the specimen will support the favored explanation.

Randomized concealed humidity challenges expose how quickly comparisons can be biased by knowing which materials received the harsher dose. The conventional chronic-interface material shares threshold definitions and ageing exposures. Every failed specimen must remain in the denominator. A survival curve becomes untrustworthy if units failing early are quietly removed as preparation mistakes or if post hoc impedance cutoffs are changed.

In the adversarial reading, the proposed effect is first assumed to be ordinary until it has disproved that convenient null. The source deliberately names apparent endurance created by accelerated-test mechanism change or excluding failed specimens as a competing explanation. This is not an insult to the candidate material; it is a safeguard against confusing an observed change with its preferred cause. The appropriate comparison is conventional chronic-interface material with same ageing dose and endpoint thresholds. Both arms need the same exposure window, handling burden, measurement budget and reporting threshold. Any later claim that the comparator was unfair should be checked against the preregistered resource ledger, not resolved by retrospectively editing the winner.

A challenge is meaningful only when its identity was hidden and its dose or geometry can later be independently reconstructed. Here the specified challenge is randomized accelerated humidity. The experimenter should plan in advance how to detect failure of concealment and how to report mislabeled, missing or noncompliant preparations. The candidate model and its strongest ordinary rival should each receive the same sealed test instances. This produces a contest between predictive accounts of the world, not a contest between storytelling styles after the outcome is known.

The explicit hard-stop boundary in this source is loss of insulation, corrosion product release, thermal runaway or unverifiable service history. A stop condition is not an editorial disclaimer. It is a causal part of the experiment because the most attractive observation may occur in a specimen that has already ceased to satisfy the integrity conditions under which the hypothesis was stated. For this chapter, the stop log should be evaluated before computing any favorable average. The point is not to make promising material development impossible, but to prevent an uncontrolled risk or a broken measurement reference from being renamed a technical success.

Future qualification requires a ledger of wetting history, humidity, temperature, corrosion products, electrical thresholds and censoring reasons. Causal interpretation remains conditional on accelerated and natural ageing having comparable dominant physics. Real implanted safety and therapeutic persistence are not established by any benchtop durability record.

The evidence package must allow another investigator to arrive at a less flattering answer. That means supplying calibration artifacts, intervention masks with an auditable release rule, excluded specimens, analysis code and uncertainty propagation. In particular, the published time-to-impedance-failure [day] should be reconstructable from raw measurements rather than copied from a graphical legend. The protocol must state which assumptions are material-specific and which belong to general experimental hygiene. This separation prevents a future laboratory from mistaking an administrative convention for a biological law.

One Research Gate can now be written as a conditional experiment rather than a prophecy: if randomized accelerated humidity is delivered while the measurement chain stays intact, does time-to-impedance-failure [day] change in the prespecified direction beyond the prediction of apparent endurance created by accelerated-test mechanism change or excluding failed specimens? INTERLUDE 3 | The temporal dimension: endurance and responsible disappearance

Materials may fail by accumulating defects or by eroding on purpose. Both routes require a time series and an explicit terminal condition. A survival estimate must include units that fail early, just as a biodegradation plot must include detached matter and the signal that ceased during erosion. Accelerated tests can inform mechanism but cannot substitute for real-duration evidence unless the failure physics are shown to transport between regimes.

Safety in time deserves more attention than a single end-of-test comparison. Self-healing, selectivity and chronic stability could all look successful at chosen snapshots. The practical scientific question is what happens between snapshots: intermittent shorts, leakage, thermal excursions, irreversible chemistry and transient loss of signal identity. Continuous or high-frequency monitoring should capture such failures, with a traceable rule for what constitutes an unacceptable event.

The long-duration narrative changes how the research result should be archived. A complete trace includes the days on which specimens were not measurable and the reasons for those gaps. A self-healing conductor that repeatedly loses and regains signal must report both recovery time and outage duration. A selective material must report false positives over its full tested history. A dissolving device must report what happened to each released component. None of these time-dependent burdens can be erased by presenting only the final specimen photograph.

The family closes by comparing two futures: a permanent device that demonstrably survives time and a temporary one that demonstrably leaves safely. Endurance and planned retirement are different strategies that nevertheless share a demand for a complete failure record.

Sometimes the correct fate of a neural interface is to disappear. Yet disappearing is not an automatic benefit. Polymer erosion can release chemical products, swell before losing dry mass, shed fragments or end a recording before its signal has been responsibly handed over. A biodegradable design must therefore make two clocks agree: the clock of useful electrical function and the clock of material degradation.

A mathematical expression earns its place by connecting measured inputs to a falsifiable output. For biodegradable neural interface nanomaterials at the limit, the output is dry-mass retention [%]; every assumed conservation relation, response function or statistical normalization should be translated back into actual instrument files. State which parameters are fixed by direct measurement and which are inferred. If a parameter is not independently identifiable, the manuscript should report a range or a model comparison rather than a false point estimate. This distinction matters especially when environmental drift and the proposed mechanism change the same recorded signal. The experiment should be designed to break that equivalence.

In the blind buffer-turnover challenge, the apparent rate of degradation can shift as the environment is refreshed. Stable reference material and a known biodegradable polymer set the boundaries. Dry-mass retention after standardized drying avoids mistaking water uptake for material survival. Degradation-product chemistry and fragment collection keep missing matter from being declared harmless by absence.

The null hypothesis here has a personality. It says that mass loss explained by absorbed water, fragment shedding or selection of intact samples can account for what looks like a specialized result. The investigators should let that rival make a quantitative prediction. A strong test compares it directly with stable reference interface and biodegradable polymer of established composition, rather than finding a deliberately weak untreated condition and celebrating an easy victory. In this framework a conventional solution that matches the candidate is scientifically productive. It narrows the mechanism, exposes unnecessary engineering complexity and tells future readers where additional evidence would actually change the decision.

Now imagine the sealed envelope containing blinded buffer turnover. In a prospective design the analyst cannot search the data to learn which assignment makes the novel explanation look best. Predictions about direction, magnitude and acceptable uncertainty must have been registered earlier. The unblinding procedure should identify not only nominal treatment but also physical delivery of the challenge, because an intervention that never reached the specimen cannot test the hypothesis. For this topic, the most useful outcome may be an unexpected null that reveals an unrecognized dependency on preparation history.

The explicit hard-stop boundary in this source is unsafe degradation products, loss of mandatory signal continuity or unaccounted material. A stop condition is not an editorial disclaimer. It is a causal part of the experiment because the most attractive observation may occur in a specimen that has already ceased to satisfy the integrity conditions under which the hypothesis was stated. For this chapter, the stop log should be evaluated before computing any favorable average. The successor's task is to predefine the last permissible recording and the transfer to a backup sensor, not merely to record when mass reaches a pleasing percentage. A material that degrades elegantly while silently removing a mandatory signal is not a successful neural interface.

The final manuscript should describe what was measured, what was inferred and what was merely imagined. This prospective family does not contain an executed blinded trial; its value is the plan for one. THE EXPERIMENT THAT MIGHT REFUTE THE WHOLE STORY

The reader enters a laboratory in which every promising material is assigned a concealed reference sample. A helpful instrument can make an electrode appear better without a single material property changing. This is why neural interfaces demand simultaneous evidence from chemistry, electrical transport, mechanics, cell response, and time. A design earns the word intelligent only if its contribution can be separated from ordinary optimization and from the artifacts of its own measurement chain.

Imagine a fully preregistered study in which the experimental group underperforms a conventional control. There is no need to rescue the preferred claim. First check whether the negative result was generated under qualified conditions: sample identity intact, instruments calibrated, disturbance actually delivered, safety boundaries respected. Next compare the observation against both proposed model and strongest rival. If the rival predicts it more accurately, the mechanistic claim must narrow. If neither predicts it, the appropriate next step is a new discriminating perturbation, not an extra adjective in the abstract.

A negative result also asks a practical question about the use of resources. The proposed nanostructure may require expensive fabrication, highly selective imaging or a fragile controller. A conventional material that achieves the same measurable performance with fewer failure modes may be a more valuable endpoint for engineering. Published research should disclose this possibility before unblinding. Doing so allows the program to evolve through elimination of unnecessary complexity instead of perpetual expansion of untested mechanisms.

The strongest successor experiment is one that can be explained in a short sealed protocol yet produces enough raw information for serious analysis. A single externally reconstructed measurement with a fair comparison can support a modest claim. Hundreds of attractive images without source identity cannot support that same claim. The tension between accessible storytelling and technical rigor is not resolved by removing mathematics; it is resolved by explaining exactly what each measured quantity does and does not mean.

RESEARCH GATES AS LETTERS TO A SECOND LABORATORY

The 200 Gates per volume and 33 Phoenix proposals are best read as disciplined requests for future falsification, not as proof of accomplished laboratory outcomes. A useful Gate states a mechanism, an adversary, a measurement unit and a failure condition. It also states who can reconstruct the result. A successor who reports that a standard platinum electrode or a commercial flexible trace works just as well has not betrayed the program; that conclusion is precisely what makes the archive scientifically serious.

Every gate must have a physical or measurable point of entry. A statement such as “will this material transform neural medicine?” is too broad to be answered by a small independent trial. A useful gate instead specifies an input, a measurement with units, a conventional competitor, an uncertainty standard and a precommitted failure condition. Its extreme speculation can be creative, but the path from speculation back to a bench-scale discriminating experiment must remain visible.

The first letter in a Gate can remember the uncertainty that produced it. The second can name a possible future that remains conditional on evidence. The third must tell an actual laboratory how to start: which samples to prepare, which nuisance to hide, how to blind the analyst, where the reference lies, what adverse event ends the run and what data package should be returned. That progression turns a literary structure into a bridge between present and future experiments.

Phoenix proposals are similarly valuable when treated as prospective evidence instruments. A calibrated coupon registry, external witness rig, blinded challenge cassette or second-site analysis repository could reduce friction for the next researcher. But none of those objects, merely being proposed, establishes that the claimed biological mechanism exists. A future manuscript should date the design, list the parts actually built, and distinguish a simulated reconstruction from an observed physical phenomenon.

THE LAST PAGE | A RESPONSIBLE RESEARCH HANDOFF

The material can only enter a neural research program as a qualified, bounded component. The books ask an ambitious question: can a system carry information without silently replacing measurement with decoration? The answer remains open; what the family contributes today is a precise program for deciding when evidence is good enough to continue and when safety requires a stop.

These volumes offer a plan, not permission to claim clinical treatment. The source materials are nonclinical research working editions. They contain equations, proposed experiments, uncertainty controls, strong conventional comparators, future research questions and speculative prototype ideas. The notebook adds interpretation for readers across disciplines. It neither certifies the original formulas nor supplies missing empirical outcomes. In particular, the existence of a proposed model does not make its parameters identified, and the existence of a bibliographic DOI does not validate a new claim.

A useful final archive would hold the exact PDF edition used, title and flagship number, frozen protocol, predeclared outcome and units, reference certificates, source-code version, blinded assignment procedure, all raw data including failures, censoring and missingness records, the measured safety stops, and a clear list of unresolved competitors. That archive would allow a stranger to begin not at zero, and not in borrowed certainty, but at a precise frontier of uncertainty.

If a future researcher reproduces only a fraction of the proposed effect, that fraction is still knowledge. If a conventional design wins, the comparison is still knowledge. If a hidden intervention destroys the attractive model, the failure is a map of what the model was missing. Scientific progress can therefore mean preserving the ability to ask the next better question, and giving the next investigator enough evidence to answer differently.

metadata.title: HEALTH FINANCING STRUCTURES AND OLDER ADULT LONGEVITY: COMPARATIVE EVIDENCE FROM SEX DISAGGREGATED NATIONAL ANNUAL PANELS
metadata.description: This analysis examines whether international health financing gradients persist within countries when explaining longevity after age 60. An unbalanced panel combines 2,685 complete country and year observations across 193 economies during 2010 to 2024. Separate female and male models include country and year effects, country clustered standard errors and Holm adjustment across six primary tests. Positive pooled expenditure associations reverse after adjustment: a one percentage point higher expenditure share corresponds to 0.065 fewer remaining years for females and 0.050 fewer years for males. Only the female association survives multiplicity adjustment. Government and household financing shares have imprecise baseline estimates, and paired comparisons provide no clear evidence of coefficient differences by sex. Excluding the sparsely observed terminal year leaves expenditure estimates largely unchanged, whereas country specific trends weaken precision. The findings refine health financing transition theory by distinguishing favorable international gradients from conditional national relationships without identifying causal transmission channels. Globally, expenditure ratios should inform benchmarking alongside service delivery and financial protection evidence rather than independently justify budget reallocations.

metadata.title: Reconstructing the glacial–interglacial biogeographic history of closely related North American Andrena Fabricius, 1775 bees
metadata.description:
Over the past 2.6 million years there have been ~52 glacial-interglacial cycles, which have had profound implications for species' distributional changes through time. Despite the ecological importance of bees, the long-term historical distributional shifts of most species have not been studied using ecological niche models (ENM) or analyzed in depth biogeographically. To date, ENM studies have been limited for bees in the genus Andrena. However, Andrena is an extraordinarily diverse group represented by > 1,700 species, offering a unique opportunity to address complex biogeographical questions through ENM. The species restricted to North America in the subgenus Plastandrena represent an ideal system for such study due to their common ancestry, occupancy of diverse environments, and polylectic nature. We utilized Chelsa-bioclim V2.1 1981–2010 and Chelsa-TraCE21k climate data in combination with the maximum entropy method (Maxent) to model the potential suitable area for each species during the modern day and Last Glacial Maximum (LGM). Our findings suggest that each of the five species potential distributions may have experienced significant expansions from the LGM to modern day, even though each species occupies distinct environments. Furthermore, we document the species-level biogeography of each taxon, identify new areas of potential discovery, and address regions where colonization may be limited by barriers such as the Sonoran Desert and species-specific phenologies. Future research should test these interpretations through population genetic studies.

Highlights

First detailed study of Andrena bees using ecological niche models with hindcasting to the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM).

Potential significant post-glacial expansions were identified for all five species from the LGM to the present even though each species occupies distinct environments.

New potential localities for species discovery are documented across North America.

Barriers to colonization, including the Sonoran Desert and specific phenologies, likely restrict Andrena argemonis and Andrena mellea from coastal regions of the Western United States.

Andrena crataegi may have undergone splitting into three or more populations during the LGM, followed by a limited reconnection during the modern interglacial period.

Our results demonstrate the unique biogeography of these understudied bee species and illustrate how dramatic glacial-interglacial cycles have driven distributional changes, underscoring the need for future population genetic research.

metadata.title: Causal Single-Cell Transcriptomic and Splicing Clocks Uncouple Molecular Damage from Protective Adaptation Across Human Aging, Spatial Microenvironments, and Rejuvenation
metadata.description: Single-cell transcriptomic aging clocks predict chronological age with high precision, yet conventional models conflate molecular drivers of degeneration (Damage) with compensatory stress responses preserving viability (Adaptation). This study introduces scCausAge, integrating 51,852 SuSiE fine-mapped expression and LeafCutter RNA-splicing quantitative trait loci (PIP >= 0.001, F >= 10) across 20 human cohorts with correlation-adjusted multi-trait Mendelian Randomization across six longevity and epigenetic aging genome-wide association studies (N > 1,000,000), identifying 3,153 causal aging loci (114 at FDR < 0.10; 404 with colocalization PP.H4 >= 0.50). Intersecting genetic causal directionality with single-cell aging trajectories across 90,683 human cortical nuclei spanning six representative subclass atlases from the 1,392,421-nuclei Seattle Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas (SEA-AD) via nested donor-grouped cross-validation uncouples causal damage (scDamAge) from protective adaptation (scAdaptAge) across 20 cortical lineages and reveals 425 cross-lineage context-flipping genes (ENO1, LIPA, KDM1B, NOVA1). Causally constrained clocks outperform chronological clocks in GABAergic interneurons (r = 0.630 vs. 0.549) and distinguish cognitive resilience from Alzheimer's dementia via preserved endothelial scCausAge (d = -0.778, p = 0.00336, AUROC = 0.690) and scAdaptAge (d = -0.536, p = 0.0262, AUROC = 0.664), as well as lower L5 ET neuronal (d = +0.586, p = 0.0247) and microglial (d = +0.425, p = 0.0384) Net Vulnerability Index. Across 650,459 MERFISH cells from 27 human brains, high-damage glia transmit paracrine damage within 30 um (p = 4.11e-13), whereas high-adaptation glia shield neighboring oligodendrocytes and neurons (p = 9.58e-11). Across external human progeria, radiation senescence, and OSKM reprogramming cohorts, maturation-phase partial reprogramming (Days 16-24) achieves selective rejuvenation (Delta scDamAge = -2.31 yr, p = 0.00965 at Day 16; Delta scDamAge = -1.85 yr, p = 0.00161 and Delta scAdaptAge = +1.23 yr, p = 0.0142 at Day 24), whereas full iPSC pluripotency erases somatic adaptation (Delta scAdaptAge = -5.56 yr, p = 7.57e-5 in Endothelial and -5.37 yr, p = 0.0163 in OPC), and Open Targets/ChEMBL screening prioritizes 16 clinical geroprotectors.

metadata.title: Selective Preservation of Past Life: Which Ecological Signals Survive in the Fossil Record?
metadata.description:
This repository contains the computational materials associated with the manuscript Selective Preservation of Past Life: Which Ecological Signals Survive in the Fossil Record?, submitted to Ecography.

The study uses present-day mammalian biodiversity as a reference to evaluate how simulated fossil-record incompleteness alters the representation of different biodiversity properties. Five sequential filters account for sediment availability, geographical range size, adult body mass, fossil-site distribution and taxonomic sampling. Three species-retention scenarios (25%, 50% and 75%) are evaluated.

The analyses examine changes in mammalian species richness across five Köppen–Geiger climatic biomes and geographical regions, richness patterns across temperature–precipitation space, functional trait probability distributions based on maximum longevity and litter size, and the relative representation of five mammalian orders: Carnivora, Rodentia, Cetartiodactyla, Primates and Chiroptera.

The computational workflow was developed in R and is organized into scripts for data preparation, sequential filtering, biodiversity analyses and figure generation. The analyses use mammalian distribution information from the IUCN Red List, taxonomic and trait information from COMBINE, climatic variables from WorldClim 2.1, sediment information from the Global Unconsolidated Sediments Map and fossil occurrence records from the Paleobiology Database.

The simulations evaluate three retention scenarios using a fixed random seed (288), with one stochastic realization per scenario. The resulting analyses describe changes across sequential filtering stages rather than independent effects of individual preservation processes.

The materials are provided for scientific evaluation and reproducibility. Access to original third-party datasets remains subject to the licensing and redistribution conditions established by their respective providers.

metadata.title: Apoptosis and Mobilization of Lymphocytes to Cardiac Tissue Is Associated with Myocardial Infarction in a Reperfused Porcine Model and Infarct Size in Post‐PCI Patients
metadata.description:
ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is the most severe outcome of coronary artery disease. Despite rapid reperfusion of the artery, acute irrigation of the cardiac tissue is associated with increased inflammation. While innate immune response in STEMI is well described, an in-depth characterization of adaptive immune cell dynamics and their potential role remains elusive. We performed a translational study using a controlled porcine reperfusion model of STEMI and the analysis of lymphocyte subsets in 116 STEMI patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). In the animal model, a sharp drop in circulating T lymphocytes occurred within the first hours after reperfusion. Notably, increased apoptosis of circulating lymphocytes and infiltration of proinflammatory Th1 lymphocytes in the heart were observed 48 h after reperfusion. Similarly, in STEMI patients, a sharp drop in circulating T lymphocyte subsets occurred within the first 24 h post-PCI. A cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) evaluation of these patients revealed an inverse association between 24 h circulating T lymphocyte numbers and infarction size at 1-week and 6-month post-PCI. Our translational approach revealed striking changes in the circulating and tissue-infiltrating T lymphocyte repertoire in response to ischemia-reperfusion. These findings may help in developing new diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for coronary diseases.

metadata.title: Global review of bull shark Carcharhinus leucas (Valenciennes, 1839) museum specimens: summary of records, geographic analysis, and assessment of their scientific value
metadata.description:
Background

Museum specimens provide critical data for taxonomy, systematics, biogeography, and conservation. Well-preserved vouchers are essential for documenting both historical and contemporary distributional records, supporting a better understanding on species distribution in a world undergoing constant environmental changes. Regarding the euryhaline bull shark, Carcharhinus leucas, voucher specimens reliably confirm occurrences in areas where the species' status was previously unclear and clarify the identity of morphologically similar shark species found in freshwater environments. This study aims to provide a synthesis of C. leucas voucher specimens, assessing their scientific significance and identifying priority regions for future sampling to address knowledge gaps in the occurrence and distribution of the bull shark.

New information

This study is one of the few available comprehensive global reviews of museum specimens for an extant shark species. By reviewing public databases and the primary literature, we collated information on 964 Carcharhinus leucas voucher specimens housed in ichthyological collections worldwide, of which 830 (86.1%) were associated with spatial metadata that allowed for geolocating of specimens. Among the specimens with spatial information, 6.3% (n = 52) were collected in freshwater, 49.0% (n = 407) in brackish estuarine habitats, 43.9% (n = 364) in marine environments, and 0.8% (n = 7) lacked precise locality so were not attributable to one of these categories. Our spatial analysis revealed several regions where collection efforts for C. leucas should be prioritized, including the Pacific and Atlantic coasts of South America, the Southwest Atlantic region of Africa, and the entirety of the Indian Ocean coast. The examination of this material confirmed the species' presence in locations where its occurrence was previously uncertain, and pre-dated its known occurrence in the Brazilian Amazon. Furthermore, our investigation revealed that some vouchers are imprecisely geolocated, either by the original collectors or during subsequent curation, highlighting the need for optimized spatial precision and caution when utilizing these data for scientific studies.

Key findings of our study new to science:

1. A total of 964 Carcharhinus leucas vouchers (excluding fossils and genetic samples) were identified across global natural history collections.

2. Critical sampling gaps were identified in the Global South, particularly along the Atlantic and Pacific coasts of Central and South America, the Atlantic and Indian Ocean coasts of Africa, and vast regions of Asia (Indian and West Pacific).

3. Distributional data do not support the presence of C. leucas north of Bahía Magdalena (southern Baja California, Mexico); records north of this limit remain unconfirmed.

4. Direct examination of material verified the species' presence in Samoa (Polynesia, Southwest Pacific Ocean) and the Azores Archipelago (Portugal, North Central Atlantic Ocean).

5. Three previously undocumented estuarine/riverine records were identified for Puerto Rico (n = 2) and Colombia (n = 1).

6. The first record of C. leucas in the Amazon River (Belém, Pará, Brazil) was pre-dated to 1903, ten years earlier than previously reported in the scientific literature (1913). Simultaneously, this specimen also represents the first documented record of the species for Brazil.

7. Historical vouchers from riverine locations currently inaccessible to migratory fish (due to anthropogenic barriers) provide empirical evidence of habitat degradation and loss of fish biodiversity.

metadata.title: Silica Wat as Hybrid Food Network with Gratitude-Economic Drivers: Religious Institutional Infrastructure for Middle-Way Restoration of Food Systems
metadata.description:
This paper specifies a hybrid community food network rooted in religious institutions: a distributed network of monastery-based sites, each combining a farm, a kitchen and free food distribution, operated by AI and robotic caretakers that hold no ordained status, supplied by donated garden produce plus purchased food that guarantees a supply floor, and recording contributions on a non-monetary gratitude ledger instead of pricing them. The network is named the Silica Wat food network: an institutional-design pattern by which a network of religious-monastery-rooted food-infrastructure nodes (Silica Wats — glass-architecture satellite monasteries operated by AGI-monks per the caretaker-not-ordained pattern) serves as a middle-way restoration mechanism for food systems. The pattern integrates five components: (i) religious institutional infrastructure — physical Silica Wats, planned for Cambodia first and eventually across the global Theravāda diaspora and beyond, each including backyard organic farm, sustainable kitchen, and food-distribution function; (ii) homegrown-amplified contribution layer — practitioners and laypeople contribute homegrown organic produce to the network, and robot-monk-operated kitchens prepare meals from contributions; (iii) conventionally-supplemented baseline — for practitioners and food-insecure populations who cannot contribute homegrown produce (no land, no time, no skill, urban-density constraints), conventionally-sourced food supplements the homegrown core, with long-term ratio shift toward homegrown over decades but no exclusion at launch; (iv) Kiitos / Kiitti as economic drivers — gratitude-economic primitives record the network's gifts where money would otherwise mediate them, a contribution reaching the ledger only through the thank it carries, whatever it carried, operating as a substrate above (not replacing) the regulated payment rails; (v) doctrinal grounding — the Khmer cultural saying "since Mother Earth gave birth to humanity, she will take care of humanity": everything required for health and longevity is available by default, and modern economic incentives have systematically obscured this fact. Three structural problems addressed: the health crisis (big-food / big-pharma incentive misalignment between profit and wellbeing), the hunger epidemic (unequal distribution from economic pressures), and the middle-way departure (modern food systems pushing toward comfort-saturation extremes via ultra-processed engineering). Critical positioning constraints (not-a-restaurant analogous to not-a-bank; hybrid not pure-homegrown; robot monks as caretakers not ordained; do not antagonize big food / big pharma; do not romanticize the past) are articulated. Three-phase implementation phasing (conventional baseline with a homegrown contribution layer, honoured in the story of each gift and never in a rate; ratio shift over 5–10 years; multi-decade homegrown-dominance) is specified. Offered as a defensive publication so that other contemplative-tradition institutions facing analogous food-system questions can adopt and adapt the pattern.

Keywords: community kitchen, food bank, religious-institution food distribution, hybrid food network, donated garden produce, non-monetary reciprocity ledger, community-supported agriculture, robotic kitchen, AI caretaker, food-system institutional design, gratitude-economic mediation, food sovereignty, alms-giving traditions, Silica Wat, AGI-monks, middle-way restoration, dāna infrastructure, defensive publication.

metadata.title: Topological Action and Exponential Stability of Composite Nucleonic Structures
metadata.description:
This treatise establishes the long-term structural stability of the proton by treating it as an active, non-linear hydrodynamic vorton lattice rather than a point-like particle governed by static linear potentials.

  • Active Hydrodynamic Renormalization: Unlike static magnetic dipoles, three-dimensional vortex dipoles engage in non-linear stretching that actively feeds energy into collective interaction fields, producing self-stabilizing mechanical feedback.

  • Invariant Core Stability: Nonlinear dynamical theory proves that invariant winding surfaces governed by the golden ratio maximize Diophantine irrationality, anchoring a robust non-chaotic core that resists external strain perturbations.

  • Stochastic Separatrix Barrier: Structural decay cannot proceed through ordinary perturbative transitions; it requires the entire lattice to be forced across a finite chaotic separatrix that separates the stable ground state from unconfined divergence.

  • Exponential Lifetime Suppression: Transport across this chaotic boundary is bounded by Nekhoroshev estimates, ensuring that diffusion out of the stable domain is exponentially slow and yields a proton lifetime exceeding experimental bounds without inserting arbitrary grand-unification mass scales.

  • Isospin Mass Splitting Prediction: The geometric width of the stochastic boundary correlates directly with the low-energy neutron-proton mass difference, linking subatomic longevity to measurable nucleon mass asymmetry.

metadata.description:
This interactive research resource enables exploration and comparison of transcriptional responses to the deprivation of ten individual amino acids: histidine, isoleucine, leucine, phenylalanine, methionine, tryptophan, lysine, valine, threonine, and arginine.

The atlas is based on RNA-seq data obtained from Drosophila melanogaster heads following three days of exposure to holidic diets individually lacking each amino acid.

The resource supports research into amino acid restriction and deficiency, nutrient sensing, amino acid-specific metabolic functions, nutritional adaptation, protein appetite, feeding behavior, sensory and metabolic plasticity, integrated stress responses, metabolic homeostasis, aging, longevity, healthspan, and disease-related mechanisms.

Interactive browser: https://giliezranevo.netlify.app/eaa-browser.html

Original RNA-seq data: NCBI GEO GSE270723

Associated publication: Ezra-Nevo et al., Current Biology (2025). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2025.09.062

Researchers using this resource are requested to cite the associated publication.
